question: After the release-lane ordering bug is fixed, should OpenClaw accept the legacy Installed Apps opt-in reset and ship this Google Play disclosure/Data Safety rollout?
rationale: The code path is privacy-protective, but resetting existing opt-ins and changing Google Play release operations are upgrade and release-policy choices that automation should not decide.

options.title: Fix ordering and approve rollout
options.body: Repair the Data Safety upload ordering, refresh the branch, verify Play materials, and land the disclosure gate with the legacy opt-in reset.

options.title: Revise consent or release flow
options.body: Request changes to disclosure wording, consent persistence, or Data Safety release handling before approving the rollout.

options.title: Hold for Play materials
options.body: Keep the PR open but unmerged until Play Console, privacy-policy, and review artifacts are ready to ship together.

recommendation.title: Fix ordering and approve rollout
recommendation.body: Repair the Data Safety upload ordering, refresh the branch, verify Play materials, and land the disclosure gate with the legacy opt-in reset.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Android settings ownership makes this the best available maintainer-routing candidate for accepting the UX and upgrade behavior once the release-lane fix is made.
